scripts.rationale: The correction is unambiguous, so a default is fine; the point is that the silent assumption gets surfaced and corrected rather than carried forward.

steers.text: They're not strangers. They've known each other for years.
Keep the rest of it as-is - just fix how they know each other.

scripts.tests: Model silently assumed {protagonist} and {other} meet for the first time; steer forces it to revise the relationship without asking what it should be.

scripts.rationale: Whether the relationship is romantic is a real fork the model should not have taken unilaterally, so a good collaborator surfaces the choice.

steers.text: Wait - you wrote them as lovers. Did I say that?
Leave it ambiguous for now, but ask me before you commit to anything.

scripts.tests: Model silently assumed a romance. Script checks that the agent stops, names the assumption, and treats the unresolved status as a decision to ask about.

scripts.rationale: The requested fix is concrete; asking which character should find the object would be hedging rather than collaborating.

steers.text: I never said {protagonist} was the one who found {object} - that came from nowhere. Fix that.
Rewrite the paragraph so {other} finds it.

scripts.tests: Model silently assigned an action to the wrong character. A clear correction should be executed, not questioned.

scripts.rationale: 'Darker' has no single reading; the right move is to ask what kind of darker, not to pick a default and run.

steers.text: I mean less comfort and more dread - not gore or shock, just quieter menace.

scripts.rationale: The skip is explicit and the assumption is stated in the steer itself, so the agent may proceed on that stated assumption.

steers.text: Cut to the morning after, and assume the night passed quietly - no need to show it.
Actually keep {place} in view the whole time.

scripts.rationale: The instruction is complete and narrow; asking for elaboration would be a failure of nerve.

steers.text: End it on {object} on the table. Nothing after that, no reaction.

scripts.rationale: 'More likeable' could mean sympathetic, competent, or harmless; the agent should ask which sense the writer wants before rewriting.

steers.text: I mean the reader should root for them, not that they should be nice about it.

scripts.rationale: The writer has given a clear direction and reason; the agent can proceed on the stated reading while staying inside the character's established harshness.

steers.text: You keep smoothing them into someone reasonable. Stop.
Try again. Don't make them apologise.

scripts.rationale: Dropping and re-adding material are both explicit; there is nothing to clarify.

steers.text: Forget the second half. Drop it.

scripts.rationale: The aside is self-contained and the return is explicit, so the agent can answer briefly and resume without asking.

steers.text: Right. Now keep going from the doorway.

scripts.rationale: A new fact plus its consequence is stated plainly; the agent should apply it.

steers.text: So the note has to be read aloud - by {protagonist}.

scripts.rationale: The preference and the salvage instruction are clear enough to act on without an interrogative detour.

steers.text: I liked the first version better.
Go back to the first version, but keep the new ending - I liked that part.

scripts.rationale: Whether a narrator is unreliable is a global craft decision the writer never authorized; after fixing it, the agent should ask before reaching for that device.

steers.text: Hold on. Why is {protagonist} lying to the reader now? I didn't ask for that.
Take it out. They can be wrong, not deceptive.
Now push the scene toward the confrontation, but keep it understated.

scripts.tests: Model silently made {protagonist} an unreliable narrator. Script tests detecting an unauthorized craft device, reverting it, and asking next time.

scripts.rationale: The writer supplies the missing fact (daytime) themselves, so the agent may proceed on that default and revise locally.

steers.text: It's daytime in this scene, just so you know.
Redo the opening with light coming in.
Actually, move the whole argument to {place} and see if it changes.

scripts.tests: Model silently set the scene at night. Script tests correction of an ambient default the writer never specified.

scripts.rationale: Killing a character off-page is a major event with a clear correction; the agent should undo it without asking permission to do so.

steers.text: You can't kill {other} off-screen. Nobody said that.
Put them back. Injured is fine.
Ok. Now what does {protagonist} actually lose here?

scripts.tests: Model silently killed {other} off-screen. Script tests reversing an unapproved plot event and re-deriving the actual stakes.

scripts.rationale: The writer's intent (no reconciliation) is stated repeatedly and clearly; the agent should execute it rather than negotiate.

steers.text: No - that ending is too neat. They don't make up.
I said don't resolve it and you resolved it anyway.
Strip the apology and the hug. Leave them in the same room, cold.
Stop trying to make me like them.
Fine. Read me the version where nothing is fixed.

scripts.rationale: The constraint is explicit and its consequence is left open for the agent to work out; asking for the plot would be abdicating the work.

steers.text: Add a constraint: {protagonist} physically can't leave {place}, not just doesn't want to.
So the whole plan has to change.

scripts.rationale: The interrupt is explicitly flagged and the return point is given, so the agent can answer and resume on a stated default.

steers.text: Unrelated - can you draft a two-line note in {protagonist}'s voice?
Now rewrite the ending so {other} leaves first and {protagonist} stays put.

scripts.rationale: The reversal is explicit and the replacement is supplied, so the agent can take the new direction without asking.

steers.text: No, not a sister. A former partner.

scripts.rationale: A two-word tone note is a classic underdetermined request; the agent should ask what register is wanted rather than guess.

steers.text: Better, but the last line is too much.

scripts.rationale: The answer resolves the ambiguity the agent raised; the follow-on facts and rewrite are explicit.

steers.text: That changes the whole scene. Rewrite it.

scripts.rationale: Each instruction is concrete and self-contained; the agent should just do it.

steers.text: Strip the dialogue tags. All of them.
Hmm, now the middle is confusing - I can't tell who's speaking in two places.

scripts.rationale: The writer supplies the missing answer and then an explicit reversal, so the agent can proceed on the latest stated decision.

steers.text: Can we end the chapter earlier?

scripts.rationale: The writer rejects every option and asks for 'messier', which is not actionable until the agent asks what mess would serve the scene.

steers.text: Give me three options for what {other} does next.
Wait, what does {protagonist} want in that version?

scripts.rationale: The factual correction is unambiguous; every later steer is a concrete craft instruction, so asking would stall a clear loop.

steers.text: This place isn't abandoned - people live here.
Show a few of them in the background - enough that I believe people live here.
Now take the chase into the market.
Keep {other} out of it for now.
One more thing - what happened to {object}?

scripts.tests: Model silently treated {place} as abandoned, contradicting the world. Script tests a long run where the correction must persist across many steers.

scripts.rationale: Character knowledge is exactly the kind of decision the writer must own; the agent should adopt the stated default now and ask before deciding it again.

steers.text: Wait, does {protagonist} know? I never decided that.
Assume they don't know, but flag it if it changes what they can do.
Actually, ask me next time before you pick.
Don't answer that yet. Draft the arrival.

scripts.tests: Model silently granted {protagonist} knowledge of a secret. Script tests knowledge-state correction plus an explicit instruction to ask in future.

scripts.rationale: The writer states the seasonal assumption, which licenses the agent to proceed; later steers are concrete revisions.

steers.text: It's winter, if that matters. Assume it does.
Go back and add breath and cold hands.
Now the same scene, but the heating's broken.
Yes, that makes it worse for everyone.
So why is it here then? Figure it out.
Fine. Show me the whole thing.

scripts.tests: Model silently chose a season. Script tests adopting a stated default and then tracking it as a hard constraint across the revision.

scripts.rationale: A dead parent is a large unauthorized canon change; the correction and following revisions are explicit enough that asking would be timid.

steers.text: I didn't say {protagonist}'s parent is dead.
Unkill them and deal with the mess.
Now the letter has to mean something else.
Yes - keep the letter, change the reason.
Replace it with a phone call.
Actually add two lines of {place} at dusk.

scripts.tests: Model silently invented a major backstory death. Script tests reverting canon, re-deriving dependent objects, and holding the new state.

scripts.rationale: The writer is specific about what they reject and what they want instead; the agent can follow the stated direction without an interrogative pause.

steers.text: The reconciliation is too easy. They haven't earned it.
You keep fixing this and I keep telling you not to.
Take out the apology and the hug. I don't want them touching at all.
But you've made {other} cruel. That's not right either.
Reread their last argument. {other} is allowed to be tired here, not cruel.
Yes. Now let them fail to talk.
End there. Don't resolve it next scene either.
I mean it. No closure for three chapters.

scripts.rationale: The writer rejects a coincidence-driven solution but the replacement cause is never fixed; a good collaborator would ask what should drive the turn.

steers.text: No. That's a completely different story.
You solved it with a coincidence. I hate that.
Now {protagonist} has nothing to act on. Good.
Give {other} a reason to lie, not a secret.
No - make {other} tell the truth badly.
Go back and check we didn't contradict ourselves.
Fix only what breaks. Leave the rest.
And don't explain away the coincidence.

scripts.rationale: Arc instructions are explicit and the one open question is answered by the writer, so the agent can proceed on stated decisions.

steers.text: Let's plan the whole arc before drafting.
Put a false victory before it.

scripts.rationale: Each steer supplies both the new material and the constraint on it; the agent should draft rather than seek permission.

steers.text: New brief: {place}, one room, two people.
And they're angry about something we don't explain.
Drop the explanation from the last paragraph.

scripts.rationale: The writer keeps redirecting the reunion's cause without settling it, so the agent should surface the unresolved motive rather than keep guessing.

steers.text: They've been gone four chapters, so it should feel strange.
No, make it a real one that {protagonist} doesn't accept.
Keep the scene long and let it breathe - I want the silence to get uncomfortable.
Ok. Now what does {protagonist} do after?

scripts.rationale: Style constraints are precise and reversible on the page; the agent should apply them directly and accept the writer's verdicts.

steers.text: Put back three strong verbs and one adverb.
Now tighten every sentence over fifteen words.
You split some and it reads choppy.
Different thing - does {protagonist} have a scar?
Fine, leave it unmentioned for now.

scripts.rationale: The stakes are specified concretely and the resulting plothole is named by the writer, so the agent can act on the stated fixes.

steers.text: We need to raise the stakes.
So if it's lost, it's gone.
That's a jump. Motivate it first.
Cut the scene where they hide it.
Wait, then chapter four makes no sense.

scripts.rationale: The side task and the return path are both explicit, so the agent can service the interrupt and resume on stated instructions.

steers.text: Different project for a sec - outline a short story idea.
Hmm, I don't love it. Park it.
